hypothesis: The user (31 Oct - 1 Nov 2026): a time-series experiment, on something more standard than the Laplace chain. A learned Markov kernel gives the WHOLE predictive distribution h steps ahead exactly: filter the past with BP (from noisy or clean observations), then apply the kernel h times. Against the standard probabilistic forecasters trained on the same data (Gaussian AR(1) with its Kalman filter, quantile MLP and quantile GRU, persistence and climatology), the kernel should win where the dynamics are non-Gaussian and data are few, and its intervals should be calibrated. Two benchmarks: (i) SETAR, Tong's two-regime threshold autoregression, the textbook nonlinear time-series model, with an exact oracle; (ii) a real series, hourly wind speed at the Horns Rev offshore wind farm (ERA5, 2015-2024), whose one-hour changes are heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis 8.8 after the standard transform). Known limitation, stated before any run: hourly wind is only approximately first-order Markov (partial autocorrelation at lag 2: -0.29), which a GRU reading 16 hours can exploit.
design: DATA. (i) SETAR: raw a' = 0.95 a + 0.4 eps if a <= 0, a' = 0.4 + 0.5 a + 0.8 eps if a > 0, standardised to b = (a - loc)/scale with loc = -0.380078, scale = 1.262109 (tools/core/calibrate_e59.py, from the TRUE kernel only: lag-1 corr 0.881, 66% of the time in the low regime, threshold 0.301 in standard units); a_1 ~ N(0, 1) in standard units as every chain of the package. Windows of L = 32; training N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), validation 1024, test 4096 windows per seed, under E59's own tags. (ii) Wind: data/e59/wind_hornsrev_2015_2024.json (SHA-256 7d55be61...f3f7e, data/e59/README.md); transform z = (sqrt(v) - mean of the training years for that month and hour) / training sd; training years 2015-2021 (61,368 h = 1,917 non-overlapping windows of 32 h), validation 2022, test 2023-2024 (windows of 32 h at stride 8 h); N in (32, 128, 512, 1917) training windows drawn without replacement per seed (N = 1917 is all of them). GRIDS: SETAR the project's 401 points on [-8, 8]; wind 601 points on [-6, 6] (spacing 0.02: the one-hour change has standard deviation ~0.23 and a sharp peak, so the 0.04 spacing would give it only ~6 cells). TASK. Forecast origin at site 24 of each test window; targets the CLEAN values at sites 25, 26, 28, 32 (h = 1, 2, 4, 8). Scenarios: 'clean' past (the observed values themselves) and 'noisy' past (each past value observed as x = e^{-t} a + sqrt(1 - e^{-2t}) xi at t = 0.2, sensor noise), on both benchmarks. METHODS. kernel: the neural energy kernel (width 16), fitted by clean-data maximum likelihood on the training windows (E58's code: em.clean_statistics then GEM M-steps, ladder to 1200), selected on the held-out clean log-likelihood of the validation windows (oracle-free; there is no oracle for real data); forecast = BP forward filter over the past (a point mass at the observation for a clean past), then h applications of the kernel on the grid. gauss_ar1: the Gaussian AR(1) kernel fitted by the same clean maximum likelihood (closed form), forecast the same way (its filter IS the Kalman filter). oracle (SETAR only): the true kernel, forecast the same way. qmlp, qgru: quantile networks reading the last 16 past values (clean or noisy, as the scenario), outputting 19 quantiles (5%, ..., 95%) for each of the 4 horizons, trained with the pinball loss on the SAME training windows (every origin with 16 past and 8 future values inside a window: 9 per window), Adam lr 1e-3, batch 256, 8000 steps, checkpoints (1000, 2000, 4000, 8000) selected on the validation pinball loss. persistence (last observed value plus the training quantiles of the h-step change) and climatology (the training marginal quantiles), the standard naive baselines of wind forecasting. METRICS per (benchmark, scenario, seed, N, method, h): CRPS from the 19 quantiles (2/19 sum of pinball losses, the SAME formula for every method), the exact CRPS on the grid for the grid methods (descriptive), RMSE of the median, coverage of the 5-95% interval, and the log predictive density for the grid methods. Seeds 0-7 (SETAR: data and initialisation; wind: the subsample of training windows and the initialisation).

predeclared_predictions.P1: SETAR, clean past: the kernel's CRPS is below gauss_ar1's at every N in (128, 512, 2048) and every h in (1, 2, 4, 8), in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds (the regime-dependent kernel against a linear-Gaussian one).
predeclared_predictions.P2: SETAR, data efficiency: at N in (32, 128, 512) the kernel's CRPS averaged over the four horizons is below both quantile networks', in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P3: SETAR, noisy past: at N = 2048 and h = 1 the kernel's CRPS (BP filter, then the kernel) is below gauss_ar1's (Kalman) and below both quantile networks', in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Wind, clean past: the kernel's CRPS is below gauss_ar1's at h = 1 and h = 2 for every N in (128, 512, 1917), in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds (the heavy-tailed one-hour change).
predeclared_predictions.P5: Wind, calibration: at N = 1917, clean past, h = 1, the kernel's 5-95% interval covers the test truth with frequency in [0.85, 0.95] in at least 6 of 8 seeds.

descriptive.D1: Wind against the quantile networks at every N and h, with no prediction: the GRU reads 16 hours and the wind is only approximately first-order Markov (partial lag-2 autocorrelation -0.29).
descriptive.D2: Every metric per method, benchmark, scenario, N and h; the oracle's gap on SETAR.
descriptive.D3: One forecast fan per benchmark (median and 5-95% band against the truth), and the coverage of every method.
descriptive.D4: Cost: training time per method and N.

implementation_notes_2026-11-01: Written with the code, before any run. (1) The BP filter in the noisy scenario starts from a standard normal law at site 1 (both series are standardised), the same for the kernel, gauss_ar1 and the SETAR oracle. (2) The clean scenario conditions on the last observed value only (the Markov forecast), interpolating linearly between the two nearest kernel columns, then h - 1 kernel steps. (3) crps_exact (the CRPS of the full grid predictive) carries about 1e-4 relative quadrature error and is descriptive only; every prediction uses the quantile CRPS, the same rule for every method. (4) Laptop timing on 1 Nov, one thread: the kernel M-step costs 1.95 s on the 601-point wind grid and 0.76 s on the 401-point SETAR grid, independent of N, so a fit to 1200 M-steps takes about 39 and 15 min; the quantile MLP and GRU take 0.2 and 2 min for 8000 steps. The whole run is therefore about 40 CPU-hours, twice the registered estimate; the job is sized at 32 cpus, 64G, 12 h on defq. The ladder and the network budget are unchanged. (5) One --quick smoke run (seed 0, small grids and budgets) checked every method on both benchmarks and both scenarios and the target-hash gate; its numbers say nothing about any prediction.
